questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It had to be a city that had "life". A city where a lot is happening where it's easy to meet new people and have fun.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, the host university is very slow but very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a "welcome session" where they provide a lot of information, which is very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It could have gone more smoothly especially the "modification period".

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Do NOT sign with Zenitrooms, but choose Enso. I had to move places during my stay as the first agency doesn't vet the people they let move in, so the people I lived with were not safe. Moved to another agency where everything turned out great.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Live in the city center, it's very nice! Be careful with the agency you choose.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a slow process as they seem very confused. They have interns helping them which can be good, but some of them did not know what they were doing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They offered to help with a lot. Onboarding etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
It was chaotic. It's first come first serve, but they didn't let me choose some of the courses.
They offer a course modification period, where I eventually got the classes I wanted but they (incoming UB) who had to change the courses were very slow and made multiple mistakes... just be aware.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be fast when selecting online, but remember there is a modification period where you can change the courses. If you choose to do so, you have to be very consistent with either writing them emails or show up at their offices to get it done.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the MA courses they offer, I've had on my bachelors, so I used my electives on the exchange.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything is by pen and paper, so make sure to bring a calculator etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Corporate finance
Finance I
Operations Management
International Economic Organization
Financial Statement Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the courses are fairly easy, so I would recommend all of them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When I had to move during my stay, they wouldn't give me back my deposit from the first place.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I personally ate out almost everyday with friends, so food was more expensive, but if you eat at home is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't participate in any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offered some things, but if you wanted something specific you had to find it yourself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on hikes etc. in the beginning of the semester (spring) because it is impossible to do when it's hot.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. People are welcoming, but they expect an effort.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be very outgoing and just enjoy. Participate in the ESN events in the beginning to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non were challenging but everything is postponed. Ex. dinner is at (earliest) 20 and everything is just later. Their mentality is very chill.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the people were very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy! The school isn't the best but everything else is great.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything is by pen and paper!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Spain is very different compared to Denmark in regards of safety! be aware of pickpockets and thieves. They will steal in broad daylight. Also, you cannot leave your stuff alone anywhere (especially not the beach).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
